 Everything you need to know for the 2026 Philly Marathon Weekend 
 From start times, cheering spots and road closures, here’s all you need to know for this weekend’s full & half marathons and 8K. 
 by 
 Violet Comber-Wilen 
 November 19, 2026 November 20, 2026 
 With Philadelphia City Hall in their sights, runners line up on the Ben Franklin Parkway for the Philadelphia Half Marathon. (Lizzy McLellan Ravitch / Billy Penn) 
 💌 Love Philly? So do we. Let’s be friends. Sign up for the Billy Penn newsletter today . 
 The 2026 Philadelphia Marathon weekend is welcoming 40,000 participants this year — its largest turnout ever. 
 The races and programming, which run from Friday through Sunday, include the TIAA Philadelphia Marathon, Dietz & Watson Philadelphia Half Marathon, Rothman Orthopaedics 8K, Philadelphia Kids Run and the free two-day Health & Fitness race expo. 
 We have everything you need to know about the weekend — from timing and road closures to cheering spots , as well as where to eat along the route and general guidance.
 The races and events 
 Friday 
 The Philadelphia Marathon Weekend Expo kicks off at the Pennsylvania Convention Center. Here, you can pick up your race bib, shirt, and registration information – but that’s not all. Enjoy vendors showcasing running apparel, gels and fuel and product samples, or attend one of the speaker series events led by various elites, Olympians, experts and motivational speakers. In order to pick up your bib, you must have your ID with you and a copy of your race registration confirmation email from Nov. 17. The Expo runs from 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. on Friday. 
 Saturday  
 The Dietz & Watson Philadelphia Half Marathon begins at 6:55 a.m. for push-rim wheelchairs, and at 7 a.m. for runners/walkers. Runners will start near the Philadelphia Museum of Art, head toward Columbus Boulevard, come through Center City into University City and Fairmount Park, and end back at the art museum. 
 The 2026 Philly Half Marathon Map (Screenshot from Philadelphia Marathon Weekend) 
 The Rothman Orthopaedics 8K begins at 10:55 for push-rim wheelchairs and 11 a.m. for runners/walkers. The course starts at 25th Street & Kelly Drive near the art museum and ends right at the art museum, with an out-and-back course along Kelly Drive. 
 The Rothman Orthopaedics 8K 2026 race map (Photo courtesy of Philadelphia Marathon Weekend website) 
 If you or your child are running any of Sunday’s races, the Health & Wellness Expo will run from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. that day. You can enjoy more speaker events, vendor demonstrations, and, of course, race packet pickup. 
 Sunday  
 The TIAA Philadelphia Marathon starts at 6:55 a.m. for push-rim wheelchairs and 7 a.m. for runners/walkers. Known as one of the country’s top 10 marathons, the course brings runners everywhere from Old City, Center City and University City to Fairmount Park, East Falls and Manayunk. 
 The 2026 Philadelphia Marathon Map (Screenshot courtesy of Philadelphia Marathon Weekend) 
 The 2026 Philadelphia Kids Run starts at 11 a.m., with the start and finish line on Spring Garden Street across from the art museum steps. Age group start times will be staggered, with 4- to 5-year-olds will run about ⅛ of a mile, 6- to 8-year-olds will run about ¼ of a mile, and 9- to 10-year-olds will run about ½ of a mile. Children can also take advantage of the Children’s Zone at the Oval on Saturday and Sunday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. This includes live music, a kids training course, a sign-making station and more. 
 How do I get there?
 There are several ways to get to the course that work for both spectators and runners. 
 If you’re in Center City and feel like walking, getting around on foot is often the easiest option. You can walk between some of the first miles of the half and full marathon around Center City, and walk over to the art museum for start and finish line appearances. 
 Additionally, many spectators use Indego bikes. These pay-per-ride bikes have an easy-to-navigate app that allow you to hop on and off as you ride throughout the city. And, for courses like the marathon that go down the Schuylkill River Trail, you can also use this to easily get between cheering spots. 
 Different bus and train lines will be available depending on race-day road restrictions. You can check for the most up-to-date SEPTA schedules here.  
 There will be detours on certain bus routes beginning at 6 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 21 and Sunday, November 22:
 Routes K-12: 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12
 Routes 16-31: 16, 17, 21, 23, 25, 27, 30, 31
 Routes 32-47: 32, 33, 38, 40, 42, 43, 44, 45, 47
 Routes 47M-125: 47M, 48, 48, 57, 64, 124/125 
 Train-wise, you can take the Market-Frankford Line (the L) to 15th Street/City Hall or 30th Street/Drexel Station to get to popular cheer spots around Center City and University City. You can also use the Broad Street Line (B), to come into the city from North and South Philly. You can also use the Regional Rail lines to connect from Jefferson and Suburban Station from Center City to Manayunk if you choose to go up there. 
 Both the L and the B start running around 5 a.m., but their exact schedules will depend on any race day restrictions and which exact stop you’re coming from – so plan accordingly.  
 If you’re driving, there are several road closures to be aware of. 
 On Friday, Nov. 20:  
 The inner and outer drive lanes (both directions) of the Benjamin Franklin Parkway will be closed between 20th Street and Eakins Oval at 9:30 a.m.
 Kelly Drive Inbound will be closed at 25th Street, with local traffic permitted to Anne d’Harnoncourt Drive
 Inbound traffic on Spring Garden Street Bridge and MLK Drive will be detoured onto 24th Street. Spring Garden Street will be closed between Benjamin Franklin Parkway and Pennsylvania Avenue. Cross traffic will be permitted on 22nd and 21st streets 
 On Saturday, Nov. 21:  
 Starting at 1 a.m., all vehicles on the race route will be relocated and “No Parking” regulations will be strictly enforced. 
 Throughout the day, access to the Philadelphia Museum of Art will be maintained via Spring Garden Street to Anne D’Harnoncourt Drive. Local access will be maintained for residents and businesses at traffic control points controlled by the police department. All streets (except Eakins Oval and Benjamin Franklin Parkway) are scheduled to be reopened no later than 2 p.m.

 For motorists planning to park, the official race website recommends using apps like Spothero and meterUP to find spaces. 
 Runner tips 
 It is recommended that you get to the start line early – to leave extra time for entry lines, bathroom breaks and getting into your corral. 
 There are several things to consider before entering the start area – you are not allowed to have water or liquid inside of your water pouches or bottles when going through security. Water vests must be carried inside instead of worn, and also must be empty. 
 The race area will have purified water stations for you to refill at once you have gone through security. 
 Additionally, bags runners bring inside must be clear. There are more prohibited items – including large bags, alcohol, coolers and blankets – that you can find here. 
 Depending on the temperature on race day morning, you may also want to bring throwaway clothes – or old sweats and sweaters you can take off right at the start line. These items are picked up and donated after you toss them. 
 Runners can enter the race start area at several designated entry points: 
 Checkpoint No. 1 (22nd & BF Parkway, southwest corner)
 Checkpoint No. 2 (22nd & BF Parkway, northwest corner)
 Checkpoint No. 3 (West side of 22nd Street, into the east side of Von Colln Memorial Field)
 Checkpoint No. 4 (23rd Street between BF Parkway & Pennsylvania Avenue)
 Checkpoint No. 6 (25th Street & Pennsylvania Avenue, southeast corner). Note: After 8 a.m., this checkpoint will only allow access into the North Viewing Area.
 Checkpoint No. 6-A (25th Street & Kelly Drive, southeast corner). Note: Closed on Saturday from 8 a.m. to approximately 11:30 a.m. Please use checkpoint No. 6 during this time.
 Checkpoint No. 8 (Eastbound Spring Garden Street Bridge Ramp @ Eakins Oval) Note: Entry into the secure zone is not permitted via Martin Luther King Drive.
 Checkpoint No. 9 (24th Street & BF Parkway, northeast corner)
 The letter on your bib number corresponds to a corral – and corral changes are not permitted. You can find a corral map for the marathon here , for the half marathon here , and for the 8K here .
 We have a separate story with a play-by-play of the marathon and half marathon courses here.  
 Spectator tips 
 We have a separate story with the best cheering spots you can use to see your runner all weekend long here. And you can find race maps here.  
 You can also use the Philly Marathon weekend’s app to track your runners. 
 If you’re planning to watch family or friends, you may be subject to security rules around bags and things you’re carrying – to be safe, avoid bringing large backpacks and handbags and if you do want to bring a bag, make sure it’s clear. 
 Alcohol, coolers, large umbrellas and other items are also prohibited. You can find a full list of prohibited items here. 
 Bicycles and scooters are also prohibited for spectators. There are certain areas outside the course where you can hop on an Indego bike to follow the course, but plan accordingly so you are riding outside the course. 
 There are also certain parts of the course you will not be able to access. You can find a list of entrances that will be protected by security here.
